name: 61-js-semver
prompt:
Write a small semver library in CommonJS (plain `module.exports` and `require`, no package.json and no dependencies) plus a command line front end. Node is on PATH.
semver.js exports two functions.
`compare(a, b)` compares two versions written as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, each a run of decimal digits, and returns -1, 0 or 1 by comparing the three fields numerically, so 1.10.0 is greater than 1.9.0. Surrounding whitespace is allowed. Anything that is not three numeric fields — "1.2", "1.2.3.4", "v1.2.3", a non-string — must throw an Error.
`satisfies(version, range)` returns a boolean and supports exactly these range forms: a bare version, which means equality; `*`, which matches anything; `^X.Y.Z`, which means at least X.Y.Z and less than the next version that changes the leftmost non-zero field (so ^1.2.3 is <2.0.0, ^0.2.3 is <0.3.0 and ^0.0.3 is <0.0.4); `~X.Y.Z`, which means at least X.Y.Z and less than X.(Y+1).0; and `>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<` followed by a version. An invalid version or a range in none of those forms must throw an Error.
cli.js is run as `node cli.js compare A B`, which prints -1, 0 or 1, and `node cli.js satisfies V RANGE`, which prints `true` or `false`. Anything else — an unknown command, a wrong number of arguments, or an input that makes the library throw — prints a message on stderr, prints nothing on stdout and exits non-zero.
Test your own work with node before you finish; hidden assertions cover every range form and both boundaries of each.
